questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the culture was not too different from Copenhagen and that I had good experiences with the Netherlands beforehand

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of administrative stuff with courses that was hard to decipher, both before and after the exchange which takes the rating down from 10-ish to 8.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult to navigate the different websites: welcome week, myuu, osiris, mastermath etc. and having a lot of different passwords and authenticators for each website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome week from Utrecht University and there was a welcome lunch for the Faculty of Science. But no assistance before the welcome week, which was placed quite late (from 28. August).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Through SSH you could get rooms in a few dorms that were on campus (in the Science Park).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen with oven, microwave, kettle and stove.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Try to get it if possible! It is hard to get because it is very sought after, but I met most of my friends through living on campus housing. Also, remember to check what kitchen appliances are in the contract. There was no cutlery, plates, pots etc. when I moved in.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not too hard seeing what courses were to offer from Utrecht, but also remember to look at Mastermath. But some courses are apparently not for exchange students (even though they are in English), and not all prerequisites are listed in the courses, so I had to change quite a few courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find courses on UU course website or Mastermath and then you send the international office an email with the courses that you want and they will let you know if you can get them or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can ask the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I couldn't take one of my wanted classes because of a prerequisite which was not listed, and I couldn't take another two because they were not for exchange students. But the rest was succesful and I was allowed to switch courses after trying one I didn't enjoy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early and ask about if the courses are for exchange students

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High level and interesting (for the most part)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took only Mastermath courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, although there was a lot less classes, only 3 hours per course per week. And there was a lot more assignments compared to math at KU. Also, almost all exams are closed book which was difficult when used to KU standards where almost everything is open book

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Systems and Control (Mastermath, UU)
Forensic Probability and Statistics (Mastermath, VU)
Asymptotic Statistics (Mastermath, VU)
Statistical Mechanics (Mastermath, UU)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed the Forensic and the Asymptotic Statistics courses. The first one was quite hands-on, looking at court cases and calculating probabilities, likelihood ratios etc., and the asymptotic statistics was quite theoretical but a good continuation of the course Stok2 from KU, where we considered types of convergence of random variables, estimators and consistency of estimators etc.

The systems and control course was very applied mathematics (probably more engineering) and I didn't like that. When you have primarily taken theoretical maths courses, it was hard to have to calculate matrices, solve differential equations and think in a very different way than normal. Also most people taking that course were Applied Maths students.

Statistical Mechanics I only took for about 2 weeks, when I had to do the first assignment I realized it was way too demanding and complex, so I dropped out of the course. The lectures I went to were interesting but prepare to do a LOT of work in this course!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Parties cost more than you expect and public transport is actually more expensive than Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: As stated before. Groceries and eating/drinking out were a bit less expensive though

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Olympos sports association and a bunch of other clubs, but I only really know about that. Also there was indepedently the ESN association, BuddyGoDutch.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend being a part of ESN and joining their introduction week, I met quite a few friends there and it was fun! I have also heard good stuff about Olympos but I never did it

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and explore the nature around Utrecht, the other cities of the Netherlands or go to parties/gatherings and have fun :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, very similar to Denmark. However it was a bit hard to find things in the supermarkets sometimes because things are sometimes not called what you think they are in Dutch or are placed other places than you are used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt meet a lot of Dutch students, but the ones I met was in BuddyGoDutch and in ESN, so probably do that if you wanna meet Dutchies :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most things are in Dutch, especially websites etc. But you get used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are a bit more friendly than the Danes, and their approach to life is very liberal, I like that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try and meet a lot of people in the beginning, but then eventually choose who you want to continue spending time with.
Try and get a place near the Science Park (through SSH), thats where most exchange students live and it will make life a lot easier being a part of the exchange community.
Have fun and experience the Dutch (and exchange life) culture, thats the most important part of the exchange!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from around the world and learning about their culture and also learning how to integrate into a whole new country. It was a learning experience and one I will always remember

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say finding the motivation to study when there was so much stuff you could do and people you could meet. But making study dates with others helped :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
